intro: Slack on a Mac works well for social media managers as the team's approval and check-in room. It does not publish posts for you, so use it to collect feedback, set reminders and schedule messages around the work. This page covers the channel setup, shortcuts and limits that matter for that job, and where Lazur fits in.
tldr: Use one Slack channel per client, and keep each approval in its own thread.
Focus a message and press A to save it. Press M to turn it into a reminder.
Channel reminders cannot be edited. Run /remind list, delete the reminder and create a new one.
Scheduled messages wait under Drafts & sent at the top of the sidebar.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a button is. Lazur circles it. It does not click it for you.

blocks.text: Most social media managers do not use Slack to post. They use it to get a yes. A draft goes to a client, a designer or a boss. The answer comes back in chat. Slack is where those answers pile up, so the setup matters as much as any one feature.
Why Slack is the approval room for social media work

Social media work runs on short deadlines. One post can need a caption check, a logo fix and a final read before it goes live. Each step arrives as a message. If those messages sit in three apps, the morning disappears into searching.

A Slack-commissioned survey of 2,000 US small business owners in 2024 found that 28% wait on status updates from several tools and people. That survey did not study social media managers. Treat it as a comparison, not a measurement of your team.

Planable's 2025 survey of 1,000 marketers points the same way. It found that 40%+ struggle with content reviews and approvals. Only 12% reported no bottlenecks. Planable is a vendor, and its survey covers marketers in general.
Set up channels for each client and approval step

Start with channels. A common setup uses one channel per client, plus one private channel for your own review. Create a channel with the steps in [How to create a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/create-a-channel-in-slack). Decide between public and private before you invite anyone.

Here is a worked example. Say you run social for three clients. Give each client one channel for approvals. Add one private channel called internal-review for drafts the client should never see. Every post then gets one thread in one place.

Avoid one giant channel for every client. Search gets noisy. Feedback for one client becomes hard to pull up when that client asks about it. Use plain names, so a teammate can guess the channel without asking you.
Approve posts in threads and save what you need

A draft belongs in a thread under the message that asked for review. Replies stay attached to the post. Keep the post and its feedback together, and one search finds what the client said about the logo.

When an approval comes back, put the cursor on that message and press A. That saves it to your list. If the approval needs a follow-up, press M. M opens a reminder about that message, so the follow-up does not depend on memory.

Saved items sit under Home > Saved. Only you can see them. Slack's help article does not give a limit on how many you can keep, or how long they stay. Treat the list as a to-do list, not an archive. Copy the final approval text into your content calendar or doc.

blocks.title: Saved items are private
blocks.text: Saved items are visible only to you. Your team will not see that you saved a message. When others need to act, use a reminder or a post in the channel.
Slack reminders for social media deadlines

Reminders are where social media work usually slips. Slack gives you a quick route and a heavier one. Use /remind for a simple reminder. For a more complex message, Slack's reminders article recommends a scheduled message template or a Slackbot task instead.
Rules that catch people out

Two rules catch people out. A channel reminder made with /remind [#channel] [what] [when] cannot be edited. To change it, run /remind list, delete the reminder and create a new one. A reminder for a day with no time arrives at 9 a.m. in your time zone.

You can change that default under Preferences. Recurring reminders repeat by day, such as every Monday. They do not repeat by hour. Guests cannot create channel reminders at all, so a freelancer needs a member to set one.

items: Write a time into every reminder. Otherwise it lands at 9 a.m.
Post the reminder in the client channel, so the whole team sees it.
Test a recurring reminder once before you trust the pattern.
If the wording changes, delete the old reminder first. You cannot edit it.

blocks.text: Say a client approves on Tuesdays. Set a Monday reminder in the client channel with a time in it. Then check the next Monday to see whether it fired when you expected. Adjust once, then leave it alone.
Schedule messages in Slack on Mac without losing track

Native scheduling is the simplest way to send a message later. On desktop, type the message, then click the arrow icon next to the paper plane icon. Pick the time. The steps are in [How to schedule a message in Slack on Mac](/how-to/schedule-a-message-in-slack).

To find the list, click Drafts & sent at the top of the sidebar. Hover over a scheduled message to see options such as editing and deleting. Open the list the morning a post should go out, and read the text once more.

Two gaps matter. Slack's help article does not say how far ahead you can schedule. It also does not mention recurring scheduled messages. Until you confirm both limits in your own workspace, keep recurring posts in your calendar.
Search Slack fast when a client asks for an old approval

Search eats more time than most people expect. Press ⌘G to search the whole workspace. Press ⌘F to search only the conversation you are in. Use ⌘F inside a client channel, and ⌘G when you know the client's name but not the channel.

Search with words that appear in the message. A post date, a platform name or the word approved works better than a vague topic. The step-by-step guide is [How to search messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-messages-in-slack).
Keyboard shortcuts for social media managers on Mac

You cannot set custom shortcuts in Slack. Slack's keyboard shortcuts page says that is not currently possible. Learn the built-in ones that fit approvals and captions. The table lists the ones that matter most for this job.

The full list lives in [How to show keyboard shortcuts in Slack on Mac](/how-to/show-the-keyboard-shortcuts-list-in-slack). Learn the five you use every day before you learn the rest.
Mistakes that waste a social media manager's week
Most lost time comes from habits, not from missing features. These mistakes come up a lot in the approval work described above.

items: Approving in direct messages. The next person cannot see the reasoning, and you cannot find it later.
Setting a reminder without a time. It lands at 9 a.m., whether or not that suits the post.
Trying to edit a channel reminder. Delete it and recreate it instead.
Scheduling a message and forgetting it. Check Drafts & sent the morning it should go out.
Leaving notifications on for every channel. Mute the noisy ones so approvals stand out.
Treating saved items as a permanent archive. Copy final approvals into your calendar or doc.

blocks.text: The numbers behind approval delays

Two outside numbers shape how I would plan this. Planable found that 40%+ of marketers struggle with reviews and approvals. The same survey found that 38% plan only one week ahead. A weekly reminder rhythm fits how many teams already work.

The Slack survey points at status checks. Its 28% figure covers owners waiting on updates from several tools and stakeholders. For a social team, that means one thread per post and one saved list, so the answer is in one place.
Where Lazur fits into your Slack day

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time.

Use it for the Slack steps you forget. Ask where the scheduled list is, and Lazur circles Drafts & sent. Ask how to save a message, and it walks you through More actions, then Add to saved. Lazur does not click buttons for you. You still make each click.

Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app. That helps with long approval replies and caption briefs. Snippets can hold the approval line you type every week. Dictation is included with Lazur.

Privacy matters for client work. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Plans and what they include are on the [pricing page](/pricing).
Slack plan limits and pricing to check first
Slack's free plan keeps 90 days of message history. It lets you connect up to 10 apps from the App Directory. If your approvals need older threads, check that before you rely on the free plan.

Pro costs $8.75 per user per month when billed monthly. It costs $7.25 per user per month when billed annually. Slack's pricing page also lists 50% off the first three months, for Pro bought online within 7 days of creating a team. That promotion does not apply to annual plans.

Billing counts active members. Anyone who takes any action in Slack within a 28-day period counts as active and is billed. Inactive paid members get a prorated credit. Review the member list before each bill arrives.

The latest Mac build dated on or before this page is 4.53.280, released November 3, 2026. Its release notes describe maintenance and security work, with no menu changes. Update before you train a team on menu steps.

blocks.title: Check prices before you buy
blocks.text: Prices and promotions change. Check Slack's pricing page on the day you buy, and compare the monthly and annual rates.
Keep notifications from hiding approvals

Notifications decide whether you see an approval at 10 a.m. or at 4 p.m. Mute channels that do not need you. Pause alerts during focus blocks. The steps are in [How to mute a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mute-a-channel-in-slack) and [How to pause notifications in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pause-notifications-in-slack).

If alerts stop arriving, work through [How to fix Slack notifications not working on Mac](/how-to/fix-missing-notifications-in-slack). Then set reminders for approval deadlines, not for the message itself. A post due Thursday needs its nudge on Wednesday, which gives the client time.
A short daily Slack routine for social media managers
A fixed routine stops approvals from slipping. Run the same steps at the same time each day, so you know where to look.

items: Open Home > Saved and work through the items you pressed A on yesterday.
Check Drafts & sent for scheduled posts due today.
Reply in each client thread. Press M on anything still open.
Set one reminder for tomorrow's first deadline, with a time.
Mute or pause the rest until your next review block.

blocks.text: What to do next

Pick one client channel and run one post through it. Use a thread, one save and one reminder. Then add the next client. Test each reminder type once before you rely on it. For step-by-step help with reminders, read [How to set a reminder in Slack on Mac](/how-to/set-a-reminder-in-slack).

faq.question: Can Slack publish my social media posts for me?
faq.answer: This page covers Slack only. Use Slack for approvals, reminders and messages around the work. Publishing happens in the tool you use to post to each platform.

faq.question: Why did my Slack reminder arrive at 9 a.m.?
faq.answer: Slack sends a reminder set for a day without a specific time at 9 a.m. in your time zone. You can change that default under Preferences.

faq.question: Can I edit a channel reminder in Slack?
faq.answer: No. Channel reminders made with /remind cannot be edited. Run /remind list, delete the reminder, then create a new one with the right time and wording.

faq.question: Can I schedule a recurring message in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Slack's help article on sending messages does not mention recurring scheduled messages. Check your own workspace before you rely on one. Keep recurring posts in your calendar until you confirm it works.

faq.question: Where do I find my saved messages in Slack?
faq.answer: Open Home and click Saved. Saved items are visible only to you. To save a message, hover over it, open More actions and choose Add to saved.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons in Slack for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur circles and labels things on your screen, and it guides you one click at a time. You make each click yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac and runs on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: How much does Slack Pro cost per user?
faq.answer: Slack's pricing page lists Pro at $8.75 per user per month when billed monthly, or $7.25 per user per month when billed annually. Check the page before you buy, since prices can change.
